search_hits.title: Parkinson's Disease: What It Is, Symptoms & Treatment
search_hits.snippet:
Medically Reviewed.Last updated on 02/17/2026.

Parkinson’s disease is a progressive condition that affects movement. It often starts with tremors, stiffness or slowness. It happens when brain cells that make dopamine stop working over time. There’s no cure, but medications and therapies may help manage symptoms to improve daily life.

Advertisement [...] #### Surgery

Surgery may be an option if medications no longer manage your symptoms or cause bothersome side effects. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is the most common procedure. In some cases, your healthcare provider may recommend Gamma Knife® surgery to help manage certain Parkinson's disease symptoms. Your provider can help determine whether either treatment is right for you.

#### Lifestyle changes and supportive care [...] Autonomic nervous system problems: These can affect things you don’t control on purpose, like blood pressure, digestion, bladder control and sweating.
 Cognitive issues: You may develop trouble with focus, decision-making or memory over time.
 Injury: Mobility issues may put you at risk of falls.
 Loss of independence: As movement and balance problems worsen, daily activities may become harder without help.
